analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Bank of America Stadium on Saturday 28 November (12:30 pm ET); if Chicago win Game 1, Charlotte must win to force a decider, and a draw goes to penalties. Charlotte beat Orlando 4-0 at home in late October and have Pep Biel (13 goals, 17 assists) and a returning Allan Saint-Maximin, while Chicago are without Rogers, Lod and Pineda. The view will be updated after Game 1.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. Charlotte's home form (4-0 against Orlando) and Chicago's leaky Decision Day defence support a high number, and whichever side trails the series will have to attack; I stay with the number until Game 1 is played.

corners.text: The site expects 10 corners, split evenly. Charlotte at home should take more than the single corner they had at Miami, while Chicago took six against Columbus; that evens out close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards and lean over 3.5. I lean a little higher for the second meeting in six days, with Saint-Maximin back from a red-card ban and Chicago booked three times in their last game; a close series usually gets more physical in Game 2.

shots.text: The site expects 28.6 shots, with 16.6 for Chicago away. That looks high for a Chicago side that had 14 at home to Columbus and is missing Lod and Pineda in midfield, so I lean lower overall.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target. Both sides have been hitting the target often (Chicago six of 14 against Columbus, Charlotte forcing six saves and scoring three at Miami), so I stay with the number.
